kurz: How couples split shared costs, who owns a child's securities account and how much tax is due on inheritances and gifts.

bloecke.md:
Money in a relationship is usually only discussed once something has gone wrong. Yet it comes down to three organisational and legal questions. What needs to be settled is who bears which share of the shared costs, who owns the wealth built up for children, and who decides and inherits if something happens to one of the partners.

All three questions can be answered in advance, usually in an afternoon. If they remain open, the statutory rules apply. These are tailored to a model that many households no longer live: a married couple with one main earner and children together. For unmarried couples, blended families and dual earners, they often lead to the wrong results. The over-indebtedness statistics show what consequences this can have. In 2025, separation, divorce and the death of a partner, at 11.1%, were among the most common triggers of over-indebtedness, behind illness (18.2%), unemployment (16.8%) and uneconomical household management (11.7%).

## Splitting shared costs

There are three basic models for the shared finances. Separate finances are particularly fair, but also particularly laborious. Every shared expense has to be split, and the lower-earning partner feels every increase in fixed costs much more strongly. A completely joint pot is convenient, but it mixes assets that should remain legally separate and means that every individual purchase needs explaining. The **three-account model** is a compromise that works well in most households. It provides for a joint account for everything shared and two personal accounts for everything else.

The split ratio matters more than the account structure. An equal split seems fair, but with unequal incomes it is not. The lower-earning partner is then left with a much smaller share of their own net income to spend freely, and therefore with a lower savings rate. A split according to income share puts both on an equal footing, because each contributes the same share of their net income.

Partner A has €2,400 net, partner B €3,600. The shared fixed costs for rent, electricity, insurance and groceries come to €2,000 a month.

With an equal split, each pays €1,000. A keeps €1,400, B keeps €2,600. A thus contributes 41.7% of their own net income to the shared pot, B only 27.8%.

With a split according to income share, A provides 40% of household income and pays €800, while B provides 60% and pays €1,200. Both contribute 33.3% of their net income, and both are left with the same percentage of headroom.

Compared with the equal split, A therefore has €200 a month more and B €200 less. Over ten years, this shifts €24,000 of saving capacity, even though the household spends the same amount overall.

bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation with €2,000 of shared fixed costs and net incomes of €2,400 and €3,600. The household spends the same in both cases.

bloecke.titel: Gift tax on a joint account
bloecke.md: A joint account that either partner can operate alone (Oder-Konto) belongs to both in equal halves in case of doubt. If one partner pays a large one-off sum into it, for example an inheritance, a severance payment or sale proceeds, the tax office may regard this as a gift of half to the other. Between spouses, the allowance is €500,000 in ten years, so this is rarely noticed. For unmarried couples it is €20,000, and the tax rate starts at 30%. Large individual sums therefore belong in an individual account and the ongoing housekeeping money in the joint account.

## Matrimonial property regime and marriage contract

Married couples who do not agree otherwise live under the [[community of accrued gains (Zugewinngemeinschaft)]]. Contrary to what the name suggests, all assets remain separate during the marriage. Neither partner is automatically liable for the other's debts, and neither may dispose of the other's securities account. Assets are only divided when the marriage ends. On divorce, the increase in each partner's wealth during the marriage is compared, and the partner with the larger increase pays out half of the difference. In addition, there is the pension rights adjustment (Versorgungsausgleich), under which the pension entitlements acquired during the marriage are divided. If one partner takes a career break for the children, the pension rights adjustment is economically the larger item and often worth more than the portfolio.

A marriage contract (Ehevertrag) has nothing to do with mistrust. It serves to regulate situations that the law reflects poorly, for example business holdings that should not be broken up, very unequal initial wealth or second marriages with children from the first marriage. A blanket separation of property (Gütertrennung) is rarely the right solution. It removes two advantages: the equalisation of accrued gains (Zugewinnausgleich), which is free of inheritance tax, and the flat-rate increase in the statutory share of the estate. It also changes the inheritance ratio. Under separation of property, the spouse and children inherit in equal shares if there are one or two children.

bloecke.titel: Statutory succession without a will (community of accrued gains)

bloecke.md: Under the law, an unmarried partner inherits nothing, not even after thirty years together. Without a will, the assets go to the deceased's children, parents or siblings. With a will, the partner inherits but pays tax in tax class III, with an allowance of €20,000 and at least 30% on the amount above it.

## Inheritance tax and gift tax

Inheritance tax and gift tax follow the same rules. Only the family relationship counts, regardless of how close the relationship was in everyday life. The personal allowances have stood unchanged in the law since 2009, even though asset prices have risen considerably since then, especially for property. Today, a terraced house in a large city can on its own use up a child's allowance.

bloecke.md:
The tax rates rise in steps with the taxable acquisition. In tax class I, the rate is 7% up to €75,000, 11% up to €300,000, 15% up to €600,000 and 19% up to six million euros. In tax class III, it stays at 30% up to six million euros and is 50% above that. The applicable rate is applied to the entire taxable acquisition, not just to the part above the step threshold. For this reason, there is hardship relief (Härteausgleich) at the step thresholds.

There are also exemptions that can noticeably reduce the taxable acquisition: household effects up to €41,000 in tax class I, a lump sum of €15,000 for estate liabilities without individual proof, and a care allowance of up to €20,000 for each person who cared for the deceased free of charge or for inadequate payment. The most important exemption applies to the family home (Familienheim). Spouses, registered civil partners and children who inherit a property that the deceased lived in personally and who live in it themselves for at least ten years pay no tax on it. For children, the exemption is limited to 200 square metres of living space. If the heir moves out earlier or lets the property, the exemption is lost retroactively.

bloecke.titel: Inheritance tax on the same inheritance for five recipients
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation with €600,000 of financial assets, without other acquisitions and without the lump sum for estate liabilities, the pension allowance or asset-specific exemptions. The differences arise solely from the family relationship.

bloecke.md: In addition to the allowance of €500,000, spouses have a special pension allowance (Versorgungsfreibetrag) of up to €256,000. However, it is reduced by the capitalised value of tax-free survivors' benefits. For people in the statutory pension insurance with an entitlement to a widow's or widower's pension, it is therefore often largely or entirely used up. The calculation above deliberately leaves it out, which is why tax is also due for the spouse there.

## The ten-year period

Starting gifts early is the most effective way to reduce the tax, and no special arrangement is needed for it. All gifts from the same person are added together over ten years (Zehnjahresfrist); after that, the full allowance is available again. It also applies per donor and per recipient. Two parents can therefore transfer €800,000 tax-free to a child every ten years. If everything is left to the will, this period never starts to run.

bloecke.titel: Tax-free transfers from two parents to one child
bloecke.unter: In each round, two allowances of €400,000 are used. The ten-year period begins on the day of the gift.

ereignisse.text: Each parent transfers €400,000, together €800,000 tax-free. The total of all transfers is therefore €0.8 million.
The allowances are available again in full, and a second round is possible. The total rises to €1.6 million.
The allowance is also available again on inheritance if the last gift was more than ten years ago. The total rises to €2.4 million.
If everything is transferred only on inheritance, the allowance is available only once, that is, €800,000. The rest is taxable.

bloecke.md:
A married couple owns €1.2 million together, half each, and has two children.

With a **Berlin will** (Berliner Testament), the spouse inherits first and the children only inherit after the second death. On the first death, the spouse receives €600,000. After deducting the €500,000 allowance, €100,000 remains taxable, which at 11% is around €11,000. On the second death, the children inherit €600,000 each. After deducting €400,000, €200,000 each is taxable; at 11%, that is €22,000 each, €44,000 together. In total, around €55,000 in tax is due.

Without a Berlin will, statutory succession applies. On the first death, the spouse inherits €300,000 and the children €150,000 each. All amounts are below the allowances, and the tax is €0. On the second death, €900,000 is to be divided, €450,000 per child. Of this, €50,000 each is taxable at 7%, which comes to €7,000 in total.

The difference of around €48,000 arises solely from the order. The Berlin will lets the children's allowance on the first death lapse unused.

- A private will (eigenhändiges Testament) that was written on a computer is invalid. It must be written and signed entirely by hand. A signed printout is not enough.
- Close relatives cannot be completely disinherited. Descendants, the spouse and, if there are no children, the parents are entitled to the [[compulsory share (Pflichtteil)]], which amounts to half of the statutory share of the estate. With a Berlin will and two children, each child can demand one eighth of the estate in cash on the first death. This is a particular problem when the money is tied up in property.
- A gift shortly before death brings no advantage, because the ten-year period does not expire before the inheritance.

The share of Berlin wills among all wills fell from 59% to 42% between 2018 and 2024. The underlying Allensbach survey gives no reasons. Possible explanations are the children's claims to their compulsory share and the higher inheritance tax from the example above.

## Wealth for children

A securities account in the child's name brings a tax advantage, because the child has their own basic tax-free allowance (Grundfreibetrag) of €12,348 and their own saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000. With an exemption order (Freistellungsauftrag) and a non-assessment certificate (Nichtveranlagungsbescheinigung), capital income of around €13,300 a year remains tax-free. Even a six-figure portfolio hardly generates distributions that high. When building wealth for a child, [[flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer)]] is therefore practically never incurred.

The drawback is that the transfer is final. What has been paid in under the child's name belongs to the child. The parents manage it as trustees and may not take it back for their own purposes, not even for the family holiday. At 18, the child alone has control over it.

bloecke.titel: Three drawbacks of a child's securities account
bloecke.md:
For BAföG, the child's own assets above an allowance are counted towards their needs and reduce the support. A portfolio in the mid five-figure range can mean that there is no longer any entitlement. The specific limit should be checked before applying, because it is adjusted from time to time.

Family insurance is subject to an income limit. If the child's own income exceeds it, free co-insurance in statutory health insurance ends. With distributing funds and large portfolios, this limit can be reached.

At 18, the child decides alone. Parents who want the money earmarked for education or housing then no longer have any legal means of ensuring this.

bloecke.titel: The early start pension (Frühstartrente) in the legislative process
bloecke.md: Under the cabinet decision of 12 August 2026, the state is to pay €10 a month into a funded retirement savings account for every child from the age of six until they come of age. Income remains tax-free during the accumulation phase, and payouts start at 65 at the earliest. In total, that is €1,440 of state money. In an illustrative calculation in which these amounts are invested for just over 50 years on average and earn 5% a year, this results in around €19,000. As of September 2026, this is a draft bill, not law in force.

## Planning for incapacity

The most common and most expensive misconception in this chapter concerns the case where someone becomes incapable of acting during their lifetime. Many people believe that their spouse may, as a matter of course, decide for them in an emergency. However, the emergency right of representation between spouses (Ehegattennotvertretungsrecht), in force since 2023, is limited to health matters. It applies only in the case of unconsciousness or illness, not when the spouses live apart, and for at most six months. As a rule, it does not apply to the bank, landlord, employer or authorities. The spouse may, however, assert claims against third parties that arise from the illness, for example against an insurer, and demand payment to the doctor, hospital or care facility. Without a [[lasting power of attorney (Vorsorgevollmacht)]], the guardianship court appoints a legal guardian (Betreuer) for everything else, and this can also be a stranger.

bloecke.titel: Decisions in the event of incapacity
bloecke.unter: Emergency representation by the spouse does not require a court order, but applies only to health matters and for at most six months; for everything else, only a power of attorney granted in advance prevents the appointment of a guardian.

knoten.notiz: in writing, original can be found

schritte.text: It determines who may act. For property transactions and bank powers, in practice it is granted before a notary or on the bank's form. Without an entry in the Central Register of Lasting Powers of Attorney (Zentrales Vorsorgeregister), nobody will find it.

It is valid in written form without notarisation and can be revoked informally at any time. It is only binding if it names specific treatment situations and measures. Wording such as “no life-prolonging measures” is too vague for this.
It specifies who should become the guardian if one does have to be appointed, because there is no authorised representative or the power of attorney is challenged.

schritte.titel: Account power of attorney beyond death
schritte.text: As a rule, it spares the surviving dependants the need for a certificate of inheritance (Erbschein) and keeps payments going while the estate is being settled.

It contains one page per area: bank and securities accounts with institution and number, ongoing contracts, insurance policies, digital logins and the location of the will. Without this list, relatives search for months.

bloecke.md: Power of attorney and advance directive come first, because they cost little and take effect immediately. Next comes the split ratio in the day-to-day household, because it shifts money every month. After that, it is the turn of the will and gift planning, as they need years of lead time. The ten-year period only begins with the first gift.

All figures in this lesson reflect the legal position in 2026 and describe model cases. With property, business assets, international connections, blended families and waivers of compulsory shares, the situation quickly becomes so complex that a notary or specialist lawyer costs less than a mistake. In addition, tax optimisation is not the top priority. A Berlin will can cost €48,000 and still be the right choice if the surviving partner would otherwise have to fight their own children over the house. The calculation allows the decision to be made consciously instead of being based on the tax burden alone.

mitnehmen: The household split ratio should follow the income share, because with an equal split the lower-earning partner's savings rate lags behind permanently.
Unmarried partners inherit nothing without a will, and even with a will they have an allowance of only €20,000 and pay at least 30% tax.
Allowances apply per donor and per recipient and renew every ten years; if everything is left to the will, they are used only once.
A child's securities account saves tax, but the money irrevocably belongs to the child, with consequences for BAföG, family insurance and control from the age of 18.
A lasting power of attorney and an advance directive take effect immediately and cost little; the emergency right of representation between spouses does not replace them.

begriffe.text: Statutory matrimonial property regime for marriages without a marriage contract. The partners' assets remain separate during the marriage; only on divorce or death is the increase in wealth achieved during the marriage equalised. On death, the spouse's statutory share of the estate increases by a flat-rate quarter.

Monetary claim amounting to half of the statutory share of the estate, to which descendants, the spouse and, if there are no children, the parents are entitled even if disinherited. It gives only a claim to money, not a say in the estate.

Written authorisation for a trusted person to make decisions for the grantor if the grantor becomes incapable of acting. It prevents the court from appointing a guardian and, unlike the emergency right of representation between spouses, also covers banking, contractual and official matters.

Joint will in which spouses appoint each other as sole heirs and the children only inherit after the death of the surviving spouse. It protects the survivor, but lets the children's allowance lapse on the first death and binds the survivor to the joint will.
All gifts from the same person to the same person are added together over ten years. After that, the personal allowance for inheritance and gift tax is available again in full.
